main_text.l: Rex dictus , nec usurpavit eum titulum , postquam
ab Octavio non nisi hanc gratiam obtinuit , ut Eth-
narcha diceretur , axiomate Regio ei promisso , ἐ-[?]τερ τὴν εἰς αὐτὴν ἀρετὴν
προσφέροιτο , Josephus lib. XVI. Antiqu. c. 10. 11. 12. Vides , quod βασιλεύειν
, Archelao adscriptum , è testamento Herodis , ne-
quaquam vero ex Augusti decreto explicandum sit.
Invertimus ergo argumentum à Saliano usurpatum.
Quo tempore Archelaus Rex dicebatur , eo Christus
ex Ægypto rediit ; atqui statim post Herodis mortem
ex apertis testamenti ejus tabulis , priusquam consta-
bat de Augusti dissensu , Archelaum Regem dixe-
runt subditi : à quo titulo postquam decretum Cæ-
saris innotuit , Judæos abstinuisse certum est. Ergò
statim post Herodis mortem Josephus cum Servatore
nostro & matre ejusdem in Palæstinam rediit.

page.notes: The page opens mid-word ("bium" is the end of "...solvere" before it); the first word is shown as "solvere" in the printed line "bium solvere", so the fragment "bium" was not transcribed as a separate word and is left out, with the paragraph marked cont="true". The Greek opening "ἐ-" at the line break is uncertain; the reading "ἐ-[?]τερ" is marked. The Greek phrase is printed across the line break, so it may be a damaged or misread form of ἑτέραν. Long s was read as s throughout. Printed hyphens at line ends are kept (Eth-narcha, Cæ-saris, consta-bat, dixe-runt, ne-quaquam). The printed quotation or indent marks („) at each line start are not transcribed as they are not text.
